$comment: Mission 1.65 Part D. The Netlas dispatch envelope. A TEMPLATE, not an action: its recipient is unknown, so no hash is computed and no approval is possible.
mission: 1.65 — Dual Enquiry Dispatch Envelope Preparation V1
subject: Technical methodology questions about public internet scan data

content_approval.why_still_valid: The bytes it names are unchanged, re-verified this mission.

why_the_recipient_is_unknown: That page carries a printed contact instruction and serves the address through an obfuscation mechanism, so automated retrieval returns a placeholder. Missions 1.62, 1.63 and 1.64 each established this. The page was not re-fetched here, because a fourth attempt would produce the same placeholder.
the_operator_action_that_resolves_it: Open that page in a browser, where the address renders, and supply the exact displayed string.
why_the_channel_is_not_evaluated: A channel is evaluated for an action, and there is no action while the recipient is unknown. Binding a route to an envelope that names nobody would be preparing to send to a blank.
why_no_hash: Contract §D6. An envelope whose recipient is unknown is a template, and a hash is an approval handle. Producing one would let an operator approve an action missing the field that decides who reads the message.
why_no_packet: Part E produces a packet only where the recipient and channel fields are known. A packet with a blank TO line is what Mission 1.64 already produced, and repeating it would add a file and no progress.
what_would_complete_this_envelope: the exact address displayed on the first-party legal page, supplied by the operator
a channel: either OPERATOR_MANUAL_SEND, or an explicit authorisation naming a connector and a sender mailbox
a sender identity, bound exactly where the channel is a connector

apparatus_state_unchanged.$comment: Part G. A question existing changes no gate.
apparatus_state_unchanged.rule: Question drafted is not answered. Question approved is not answered. Question sent is not answered. Only a reviewed first-party response may move a methodological gate.
